events.text: {npc} visits with a jar of pickled radish and a story. In the family version, {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, once pulled you out of a frozen river. You remember the river. You remember who pulled whom. {npc} tells it with great pride, and the radish is excellent.

effects.log: You nod in the right places. A good story is a kind of grave marker. You will not kick it over.
{npc} listens, frowns, then laughs. "So you were the one who got wet." The family will not believe {him}.

choices.text: Add a detail that makes {ancestor} braver

effects.log: By the time you finish there is a wolf on the ice as well. {npc} writes it down. The wolf will outlive you both.

events.text: In {npc}'s family you are the villain. {He} says so at your gate, quite politely. The story goes that you ruined {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, out of spite. Children of the line are told to finish their rice or you will come for it. {npc} wanted to see the monster once. You are holding a watering can.

effects.log: {npc} drinks one cup, then two. On the way out {he} says the monster pours too much sugar. It is a start.

ok.log: You leave out nothing, including your own part. {npc} is quiet a long time. "Nobody told it like that."

fail.log: Every word sounds like an excuse, even the true ones. {npc} bows stiffly and goes.

choices.text: Water the plants and say nothing

effects.log: Let the family have its monster. Monsters keep children eating. You water the radishes.

events.text: {npc} asks you to the family shrine. {ancestor}'s tablet stands in the middle. Beside it hangs a painting of you, commissioned long ago from someone who had never seen you. You have three eyes in it and a beard to your knees. The family bows to it twice a year.

effects.log: You bow. The painting looks wiser than you. {npc} looks very pleased.

choices.text: Offer to sit for a new one

effects.log: The new painter is honest and slow. The family hangs both. The old one gets more incense.
"So you could watch over us," {npc} says. There is no answer to that. You stop asking.

events.text: Children of {npc}'s village skip rope to a rhyme. It has your name in it, and {ancestor}'s, and a quarrel over a duck. {npc} apologises. Nobody knows what the duck means any more. You do. It was a very good duck.

effects.log: The verse about the duck's revenge goes in. The children shriek. The rhyme is complete now, for whatever that is worth.
You miss on the fourteenth jump. The children are merciless. {npc} laughs until {he} has to sit down.

choices.text: Tell {npc} the story of the duck

effects.log: {npc} listens with the face {ancestor} used to make. Some things are inherited that nobody wrote down.

events.text: {npc} has written the family history at last, bound in blue thread. There is a chapter about you. You are taller in it, and you won every fight. {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, is in it too, with a heroic death that is not how it happened. {npc} watches your face as you read.

effects.log: "It reads well," you say. That is true. {npc} glows. The heroic death will be read for a century.
You write the true death in the margin, small and plain. {npc} reads it twice and does not cross it out.

choices.text: Correct only the parts about you

effects.log: You lose four fights in the margins. {npc} says you are the first hero ever to ask to be smaller.

events.text: {npc} kneels at your gate in the rain. {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, always said you were the one worth learning from. {He} has walked nine days to ask. {His} knees are muddy and {his} chin is set exactly the way {ancestor}'s used to be.
events.arc: At Your Gate in the Rain

effects.log: A year of mornings. {npc} learns slowly, then all at once, like the one before. Teaching is remembering with your hands.

choices.text: Give {him} a breathing manual and send {him} home

effects.log: You find your old copy and press it on {npc}. "Read it twice. Then come back." It means no. It also means maybe.

choices.text: Test {him} first: hold the stance till dusk

ok.log: {npc} holds it, shaking, until the lamps are lit. You teach {him} one form. {He} cries a little. So, nearly, do you.

fail.log: {npc} falls at noon. You help {him} up and send {him} home with an umbrella. {He} does not look back.

events.text: {npc} stands in your courtyard with a drawn sword. {He} has been told, all {his} life, what you did to {ancestor}, {anc_rel}. {He} has trained for it. {His} sword is good and {his} footwork is bad, and {he} is shaking.

ok.log: You take the sword without drawing blood and hand it back. {npc} stares at it. "That is what {ancestor} said you would do."

fail.log: You are slower than you were. The edge finds your sleeve and the arm under it. {npc} runs. (-8 health)

effects.log: The cut is shallow. {npc} looks at the blood on the blade and drops it. "Why did you let me?" Because it was owed, perhaps.

choices.text: Tell {him} what the grudge was really about

effects.log: It was about a borrowed horse, and pride on both sides. {npc} sheathes the sword. {He} looks cheated.

events.text: {npc} brings a cloth pouch and an old ledger. {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, borrowed from you once and never paid it back. The line keeps its debts. The entry is {anc_years} years old and the handwriting is terrible.

effects.log: Eight taels, counted twice. {npc} crosses out the entry with real satisfaction. The ledger is clean.

choices.text: Refuse it: the debt was paid in other ways

effects.log: {npc} argues for an hour. You win, barely. {He} writes "paid" in the ledger and underlines it three times.

choices.text: Tell {him} to lend it to someone who needs it

effects.log: "Then it is your debt now," you say. {npc} thinks about that all the way home.

events.text: {npc} arrives with an abacus. By the family ledger you owe {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, three taels from {anc_years} years ago. With interest, {npc} explains, that is a small province. {He} is willing to settle for less. {He} is not smiling.

choices.text: Pay three taels, not one copper more

effects.log: You count out three taels. {npc} counts them twice. "The interest?" You point at the gate. {He} goes, but writes something down.

choices.text: Pay ten and call it closed (10 taels)

effects.log: {npc} pockets it and tears the page out of the ledger in front of you. The tearing sounds like forgiveness, almost.

choices.text: Argue the interest bead by bead

ok.log: By evening the abacus says {npc} owes you two coppers. {He} pays them, furious, and you suspect, a little impressed.

fail.log: {npc} is better at sums than you. You lose six taels and an afternoon. The abacus clicks like a laugh.

events.text: {npc} brings a challenge written in {ancestor}'s hand: a bout that you and {anc_rel} once promised each other and never fought. Something always came up. A wedding, a war, a death. {npc} has come to finish it, for the family's honour. {He} bows very correctly.

ok.log: Fifty exchanges, and you win the last one. {npc} bows low. "{ancestor} would have lost too," {he} says. "Grandly."

fail.log: {npc} wins, fairly. You laugh out loud. {ancestor} would have been insufferable about this for a decade.

choices.text: Declare it a draw, {anc_years} years late

effects.log: You write "draw" under the old challenge and sign it. {npc} adds {his} seal for the family. The paper is finished.

choices.text: Fight with a broom, as a joke

effects.log: {npc} is offended for three moves and laughing by the tenth. The broom loses. Honour is satisfied, somehow.

events.text: {npc} unwraps {ancestor}'s sword. There is a notch near the guard, deep as a thumbnail. {npc} says the family believes a demon made it. You made it. Long ago, you and {anc_rel} were arguing, and the argument got out of hand.

choices.text: Tell {him} the truth of the notch

effects.log: {npc} runs a thumb over it. "An argument," {he} says. "About what?" You cannot remember. That is the worst part.

choices.text: Hone the blade with your qi

effects.log: The steel drinks your qi and rings clean. You leave the notch. Some damage is part of the sword.
It is more or less true. You were quite a demon then. {npc} wraps the sword back up with reverence.

events.text: {npc} found a letter in {ancestor}'s things, addressed to you, never sent. The seal is unbroken after {anc_years} years. {npc} did not open it. {He} holds it out with both hands, the way you would hand over something hot.

effects.log: It says three things. One of them you will never repeat to anyone. You fold it very small.
The letter is mostly complaints about weather and one line that stops your voice. {npc} finishes it for you.

choices.text: Burn it unread at the grave

effects.log: Whatever {ancestor} wanted to say has gone the way {anc_rel} went. Smoke is a kind of reply.

events.text: {npc} brings a recipe in {ancestor}'s handwriting: a soup of bones, radish and too much pepper. The family cannot make it right. Something is missing. {npc} thinks you might know. You do. {ancestor} always spat in it for luck. That is not something to write down.

choices.text: Cook it together, minus the spitting

effects.log: It is close. It is not right. {npc} says it is perfect. You both lie a little and eat two bowls.
{npc} is horrified, then thoughtful. Next winter the family soup is said to have improved.
It is better soup. It is a different soup. {npc} writes your name next to the line, in smaller letters.

events.text: {npc} wears a plain wooden hairpin, worn smooth. You carved it. You gave it to {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, on a day you both remember differently. It has gone down the line from hand to hand. Nobody in the family knows where it came from.

effects.log: Some gifts should stop belonging to the giver. This one has. You let it go a second time.
{npc} takes it out and looks at it as if it were new. "It is not very good," {he} says, kindly. It was not.

choices.text: Carve one for {npc}'s own little one

effects.log: Your hands are older and the cut is better. The line now has two of your hairpins and no idea why.

events.text: {npc} has found {ancestor}'s training notes. Nobody can read them. The hand is terrible and half the words are private jokes. You can read them. One of the jokes is about you, and it is not kind, and it is very funny.

choices.text: Transcribe the notes for the family

effects.log: It takes a month. {npc} gets a clean copy. You keep the joke out. Some things belong to the dead.
{ancestor} saw something in the third form that you missed for a century. You sit very still for a while.
{npc} laughs so hard {he} has to lie down. "I see why you two were close," {he} says. Close is one word for it.

events.text: A young person stops you at the well. You call {him} by {ancestor}'s name before you can stop yourself. It is {npc}, {ancestor}'s {anc_gen}. The same ears. The same way of standing with one hip out. {npc} has been called that name by old people all {his} life.

effects.log: {npc} says it with patience. You say it back twice so it sticks. It does not quite.
For a breath it is {anc_years} years ago. Then {npc} sneezes, and it is not.

choices.text: Tell {him} the name is a compliment

effects.log: "Everyone says that," {npc} says. "Nobody says why." You tell {him} why. It takes the afternoon.

events.text: At a festival you hear a laugh across the square: {ancestor}'s laugh, short, then a snort. It is {npc}. {He} has no idea {he} is wearing a dead person's laugh like a borrowed coat. The fireworks go up. You stand there holding a skewer of rice cake.

effects.log: {npc} offers you some rice cake. You already have some. You take it anyway.
The fireworks end. The laugh goes on, two more times, then the crowd takes it. That was enough.
It takes a terrible joke about a goat. The laugh comes. You are not proud of the joke. You are proud of the laugh.

events.text: {npc} is the age {ancestor} was when you last saw {anc_rel} alive. You realise it at supper. Then you realise you remember the face better from {npc} than from the one who died. Memory has quietly swapped them. It is {anc_years} years. Of course it has.

ok.log: It comes back, all at once: the scar, the crooked tooth, the look before a lie. You hold it and do not let go.

fail.log: Only {npc}'s face comes. You let it. Perhaps that is what a line is for.

effects.log: {npc} listens, puzzled and kind. "Then remember me well," {he} says. "I will need it later."
The soup is good. Grief is not hungry tonight. You are.

events.text: The line of {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, has come down in the world. {npc} sells straw sandals at a crossroads. {His} fingers are quick and cracked. When {he} hears your name {he} stands up too fast and knocks the whole stack over.

effects.log: You walk away with forty sandals. You give them to a roadside temple. Nobody needs to know about this, so you tell nobody.

choices.text: Help {him} pick them up and talk

effects.log: {npc} tells you how the money went: a flood, a bad son, a worse magistrate. Nothing dramatic. That is how it usually goes.

choices.text: Teach {him} one move to protect the stall

effects.log: {npc} learns it in an afternoon. The next thug who kicks the stall ends up in the ditch. The sandals are untouched.

events.text: A magistrate's procession blocks the road: drums, banners, a palanquin. The name on the banner is {npc}'s. The line of {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, has risen high. The curtain lifts. {npc} sees you standing in the dust with the peasants, and the whole procession stops.

effects.log: {npc} hesitates, then lowers the curtain. That night a servant brings you a jar of very good wine and no note.
{npc} climbs out of the palanquin, to the horror of everyone, and bows to you in the road. The peasants talk about it for a year.
You say it quietly: a thatched house, a muddy field. {npc} does not like hearing it. Next year the taxes here go down.

events.text: {npc} is a sect elder now, with a seat in the hall and a voice people lower theirs for. {He} comes to you in plain clothes, alone, to ask how {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, would have handled a quarrel that is splitting the sect. You are the only one left who would know.

effects.log: {ancestor} would have shouted, then given in, then held it over everyone for years. {npc} takes the middle part.

choices.text: Say what you would do instead

ok.log: Your way works. The quarrel ends with nobody losing face. {npc} takes the credit, which is correct.

fail.log: Your way half works. The quarrel limps on. {npc} thanks you anyway and goes to try shouting.

choices.text: Tell {him} to stop asking the dead

effects.log: "{ancestor} is not on your council," you say. "You are." {npc} looks younger for a moment, then older.

events.text: Under a bridge you find {npc}, {ancestor}'s {anc_gen}, sleeping on straw. The family house was sold, then the family. {npc} is the last. {He} recognises the surname you say, but not you. Nobody has said {ancestor}'s name to {him} in years.

choices.text: Get {him} work and a room (8 taels)

effects.log: A room above a dyer's shop and a job stirring the vats. {npc}'s hands are blue for a year. {He} does not complain once.

choices.text: Share a meal and the old stories

effects.log: You buy dumplings and tell {npc} who {ancestor} was. By the end {he} is sitting up straighter. Names are food too.

choices.text: Slip silver into {his} sleeve and go (3 taels)

effects.log: {npc} will find it in the morning and not know who. Let {him} think {ancestor} sent it. In a way, {anc_rel} did.

events.text: {npc} has founded a clan. The banner is new silk and the hall still smells of fresh cedar. The crest is {ancestor}'s old mark, made grand. {npc} wants your name on the founding stone as witness. The stone carver is already waiting.

effects.log: Your name goes under {npc}'s, small. In two hundred years scholars will argue about it. Let them.

choices.text: Ask them to carve {ancestor}'s name instead

effects.log: "It was {ancestor}'s line before it was your clan," you say. {npc} nods. The carver sighs and starts over.

choices.text: Give the hall a blessing of qi

effects.log: The cedar beams hum faintly when you finish. The clan will say the founding was auspicious. It was, a little.

events.text: {npc} sits on your step and asks, without preamble, what {ancestor} was really like. Not the shrine version. Not the story version. Just {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, as you knew them. {He} has brought rice wine and is prepared to wait.

effects.log: Stubborn. Generous with everything but praise. Afraid of geese. {npc} writes nothing down. {He} wants to keep it the way you said it.
You tell the good years. {npc} drinks to each one. Maybe the rest can wait for the next {anc_gen}.

choices.text: Show {him} instead: a stance, a habit

effects.log: You stand the way {ancestor} stood, chin forward. {npc} bursts out laughing. "That is how my father stands."

events.text: {npc} does not like you, and says so, and then asks anyway. The family says {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, was wronged by you. {npc} wants to hear it from the other side once, to be fair. {He} keeps both hands on the table where you can see them.

effects.log: It costs more than you expected to say it plainly. {npc}'s hands relax. "Thank you," {he} says, as if it hurt {him} too.

ok.log: You say it carefully, without heat. {npc} is silent, then nods once. Two-sided grief is still grief.

fail.log: It comes out as blame. {npc} stands. "So the family was right." The door closes softly, which is worse.

choices.text: Say it was too long ago to matter

effects.log: {npc} looks at you as {ancestor} once did. It has been {anc_years} years and it still matters. You knew that.

events.text: {npc} asks you, puzzled, whether {ancestor} was a real person. The line has forgotten everything but the name. There is no tablet, no grave, no story. Everyone who knew {anc_rel} is gone, except you. You realise you are the whole archive now.

effects.log: It takes three evenings. {npc} writes it all down. {ancestor} is real again, on paper, which is something.

choices.text: Commission a tablet for the family (6 taels)

effects.log: A plain tablet of pine with the name carved deep. {npc}'s little ones bow to it without knowing why. That will do.
Some people are better kept than told. You will carry {ancestor} a while longer, quietly.

events.text: {npc} asks you to come to {ancestor}'s grave on the day of the dead. You stand together on the hill. The mound has sunk and the grass is long. {npc} has brought a sickle and a bottle. You have brought nothing. You did not think you would come.

effects.log: An hour of work, side by side, without much talk. The mound looks loved again. So, a little, do you.

choices.text: Pour the wine and speak to {ancestor}

effects.log: You tell {anc_rel} about the {anc_gen}. {npc} pretends not to listen. The wind takes most of it.

choices.text: Plant a pine at the head of the grave

effects.log: A small pine, three hands high. In a century it will shade the hill. You might see that.

events.text: On a hillside you find {npc} bowing earnestly to a grave. It is not {ancestor}'s. It belongs to a salt merchant. The family lost the real one {anc_years} years ago and picked the nearest likely mound. {npc} has been bowing to the salt merchant for twenty years.

choices.text: Tell {him} gently, and show {him} the right one

effects.log: The right grave is two hills over, under brambles. {npc} weeps, then laughs, then apologises to the salt merchant.

choices.text: Say nothing: the bowing still counts

effects.log: Bowing is bowing. You suspect {ancestor} would find this extremely funny. The salt merchant seems well cared for.

choices.text: Bow to the salt merchant as well

effects.log: {npc} looks at you strangely. You both bow. Somewhere a salt merchant is having an excellent afterlife.

events.text: {npc} is marrying into the sect you trained in, long ago. {He} comes to ask your blessing, nervously. The sect has changed its gate, its robes and its manuals, but not its kitchen. {npc} says the cook still makes the terrible bean porridge. {He} cannot understand why you are so moved.

choices.text: Give your blessing and a gift (5 taels)

effects.log: You send a pair of good teacups. {npc} writes that the elders recognised your name and stood up. All of them.

choices.text: Warn {him} about the third elder's office

effects.log: The third elder's office is haunted, or was. {npc} thanks you. The advice turns out to be still useful.
You were punished with that porridge for a year. {npc} laughs. At the wedding {he} serves a bowl to you, with ceremony.

events.text: The sect you once trained in sends word: a new disciple, {npc}, says {his} family descends from {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, and that you will vouch for {him}. The elders do not believe it. You have never met {npc} in your life. {He} is very good at lying, and very hopeful.

effects.log: You write the letter. {npc} is admitted. It turns out the family claim is true. {He} did not know that either.

ok.log: One look and you know. The jaw, the stubbornness. You vouch at once. {npc} is far more surprised than you.

fail.log: You cannot tell. {npc} is admitted on talent alone, which is better anyway.

choices.text: Tell the elders to judge {him} on talent

effects.log: "Blood is not a technique," you write. The elders agree, and test {npc} twice as hard. {He} passes.

events.text: {npc}'s family keeps a saying: there is a drop of your blood in the line, through {ancestor}, {anc_rel}. Whether it came by birth, by a blood oath or by a transfusion of qi on a battlefield, nobody remembers. {npc} has your stubbornness, everyone agrees. {He} would like to know if it is true.

choices.text: Say it is true, whichever way it came

effects.log: {npc} grins. The family will be insufferable about this. So, quietly, are you.

ok.log: There it is: your qi's old shape, faint as a watermark. You show {npc} how to breathe with it. It knows the way.

fail.log: {npc}'s meridians are a stranger's. Or yours have changed. After {anc_years} years, both are possible.

effects.log: "Then where did I get it?" {npc} demands, stubbornly. You do not answer, stubbornly.

events.text: {npc} has a new baby and has named it after you. {He} brings the bundle to show you. The baby looks at you with the deep, unimpressed eyes of all babies, then sneezes. {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, would have found this hilarious. You are trying very hard not to cry.

effects.log: It is heavier than it looks and warm as bread. It grabs your beard, or your sleeve, and does not let go.

choices.text: Tie your jade pendant to the swaddling

effects.log: You tie your old jade on with a red thread. It looks better there. Some things should go down the line.
"Because {ancestor} always said your name when things went wrong," {npc} says. "As a curse, mostly. But fondly."

events.text: {npc}'s child has a fever that will not break. The village healer has given up. {npc} comes to you because {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, always said you knew things. You do. Some of them are even about medicine.

ok.log: Three nights of needles and broth. On the fourth morning the child asks for rice. {npc} sits down in the doorway and cannot get up.

fail.log: You hold it at bay. It breaks on its own a week later. You helped. You are not sure how much.

choices.text: Push your qi into the child's meridians

effects.log: The fever goes into you instead. You lie down for a week. The child does not. That is the trade.

choices.text: Pay for a city physician (8 taels)

effects.log: The physician is expensive and arrogant and very good. The fever breaks. {npc} pays you back in eggs for a year.

events.text: {npc} mentions, in passing, that it has been {anc_years} years since {ancestor} died. You did not know it was that long. You thought ten, maybe twenty. {npc} looks at you strangely. To {him} {ancestor} is a name on a tablet. To you, it was last spring, more or less.

effects.log: {anc_years} years. You turn it over like a stone. It does not get lighter. It gets smoother.
The living deserve your attention more than the count. {npc} talks about a stubborn ox and a girl at the market. It is a good hour.

choices.text: Go and train until you forget the number

effects.log: It does not work. The number is waiting for you at the end, patient as a creditor.

events.text: {npc} is old now. Grey at the temples, a cough in winter. You knew {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, and now you watch the {anc_gen} age past you. {npc} jokes that you will bury {him} too. It is not entirely a joke, and you both know it.

effects.log: {npc} refuses it, with {ancestor}'s exact scowl. "Give it to someone with plans." You find you have plans.

choices.text: Promise to look after the line

effects.log: You promise. {npc} nods as if receiving a delivery. You have made this promise before. You keep making it.
You laugh together until {npc} coughs. Then you pour the tea. Some things are only bearable with tea.

events.text: You dream of {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, standing in a doorway. When you get close the face turns into {npc}'s. You wake before dawn. That afternoon {npc} turns up at your door for no reason, saying {he} just felt like visiting.

effects.log: {npc} goes pale, then says {he} dreamed of a doorway too. Neither of you says anything for a while. Then you eat.
You make lunch. {npc} eats like {ancestor} did, too fast, elbows out. The dream fits itself in somewhere.
The smoke goes straight up on a windless day. {npc} says that means something. You let it mean something.

events.text: {npc}'s little one hides behind {his} leg and stares at you. You do the coin trick {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, taught you a lifetime ago: the coin vanishes and turns up behind an ear. The little one shrieks. {npc} stops dead. "Where did you learn that? That is our family trick."

choices.text: Teach the little one the trick

effects.log: The child drops the coin eleven times and then gets it. The trick goes down the line again. It always does.

choices.text: Tell {npc} who taught it to you

effects.log: "{ancestor} taught you?" {npc} says. "Then you taught {ancestor} the one with the cup." You did. Lines braid.
The little one believes you completely. {npc} rolls {his} eyes. Some lies are just good manners toward children.

events.text: {npc} is about to make the mistake {ancestor} made: leave everything to follow a famous master into a war that will not need {him}. {He} is packing. {He} is excited. You have seen this exact face, at this exact age, {anc_years} years ago.

effects.log: {npc} listens. {He} unpacks, slowly. Then {he} packs again, for somewhere smaller and nearer. It is a start.

choices.text: Let {him} go: it was {ancestor}'s choice too

effects.log: Every life has to make its own mistakes. You give {npc} a salve for the road. {He} will need it.

ok.log: {npc} cannot touch you in a hundred moves. {He} sits in the dust and thinks. The war goes on without {him}.

fail.log: {npc} lands one. You let {him} go. {He} is readier than {ancestor} was. That may be enough.

events.text: One of {npc}'s elders has died, and the family asks you to speak at the funeral. You are the only one present who also knew {ancestor}, {anc_rel}. Everyone looks at you as if you were a book about to be opened.

choices.text: Speak about {ancestor}, and the line since

effects.log: You talk about how the stubbornness came down, and the laugh, and the ears. The mourners laugh through tears. That is the job.

choices.text: Speak only of the one who died

effects.log: You keep it short. It is their day, not {ancestor}'s. {npc} grips your hand afterward and does not let go.

choices.text: Say nothing; just stand with the family

effects.log: Silence from the oldest person in the room says a great deal. Nobody tries to fill it.

events.text: Local thugs are leaning on {npc}'s family: a fee for the well, a fee for the road. {npc} would rather die than ask you for help. {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, was the same. You find out from a neighbour, which is how {ancestor} always made you find out too.

ok.log: A short visit. The thugs relocate to another county. {npc} never learns why. That is how {ancestor} would have wanted it.

fail.log: There are more of them than the neighbour said. You win, slowly and painfully. (-8 health)

effects.log: Three evenings of practice in the barn. {npc} handles it. {He} is unbearable about it for a month.

ok.log: A few polite words about the magistrate's own grandfather. The thugs are arrested by noon.

fail.log: The magistrate smiles and does nothing. You will have to come back with less politeness.

events.text: Two branches of {ancestor}'s line are quarrelling over the old house. {npc} speaks for one side. Both sides want you to judge, because you are the only one who remembers what {anc_rel} actually said about it. You remember. {ancestor} said to burn it down.

ok.log: East wing, west wing, the kitchen shared. Nobody is happy, which is how you know it is fair.

fail.log: Both sides leave angry, and both blame you. {npc} sends a stiff letter. The house stands empty for a year.

effects.log: Silence. Then someone laughs. Then everyone. They sell the house and buy a feast. {ancestor} would approve.
{npc}'s branch gets the house. The other branch gets a grudge against you. Lines remember.

events.text: {npc} flies a kite on the new year with your name painted on it, under {ancestor}'s. It is a family custom, {he} explains: the names of those to be remembered go up into the wind. You did not know you were one. You assumed they had forgotten you.

effects.log: The kite pulls like a living thing. Two names, up there in the cold blue. One of you is still here to feel it.
"I am not dead," {npc} protests. "Not yet," you say. "But I will remember you." {He} lets the name stay.

choices.text: Cut the string and let it go

effects.log: The kite goes over the hills. {npc} gasps, then nods. That is how the custom ends. You just did not know it.

events.text: {npc} has started visiting on the same day every year, the day {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, died. {He} brings the same cheap wine {ancestor} liked. {He} drinks it, you pour the tea, and you say almost nothing. It has become one of the best days of your year.

choices.text: Pour, and say nothing, as usual

effects.log: The wine, by {npc}'s face, is still terrible. The silence is still good. The day goes the way it should.
You tell {npc} the thing you have never told anyone about {ancestor}. {npc} pours you another cup of tea. Neither of you mentions it again.
{npc} tastes it, frowns, and pours it out. "It has to be the bad one." Of course it does.

events.text: The inn at the pass has {ancestor}'s name over the door. {npc} runs it now, {ancestor}'s {anc_gen}. The noodles are the same noodles {anc_rel} used to burn. These are not burned. You feel oddly disappointed.
events.arc: The Inn With the Old Name

choices.text: Ask {npc} to burn a bowl, for old times

effects.log: {npc} looks at you as if you were mad, then does it. It tastes exactly right. You leave a big tip.

choices.text: Stay the night and hear the gossip

effects.log: Inns know everything. {npc} knows more. By morning you know which sects are rising and whose sons are fools.
You leave before anyone asks your name. The sign creaks in the wind like someone you used to know.

events.text: The ferry hand poling you across the river is {npc}, {ancestor}'s {anc_gen}. You know it from the hands. {ancestor} had those hands, square and scarred. Halfway across {npc} asks why you keep staring at {his} hands.

effects.log: {npc} poles slower to hear the end. On the far bank {he} refuses your fare. You leave it on the bench anyway.

choices.text: Take the pole and show {him} a better stroke

effects.log: Your stroke is better. {npc} admits it, grudgingly, which is also inherited.

choices.text: Say {he} has good hands and look away

effects.log: The river is wide and quiet. You let it be the one that speaks.

events.text: A stone bridge bears a donor's tablet. {ancestor}'s name is near the top. {npc} is scrubbing the moss off it, as the family does once a year. {He} looks up and asks if you are lost. You are not lost. You are standing exactly where you were standing when {ancestor} paid for this bridge.

effects.log: The names come clean one by one. Some you knew. Most you did not. {npc} offers you a rice ball. You take it.
{npc} does not know. You do: a child drowned here once, and {anc_rel} could not stand it. You tell {npc} that.
The bridge holds, as {ancestor} meant it to. That is the whole point of a bridge.

events.text: A bandit steps out with a rusted saber and demands your purse. {He} gives {his} name to sound frightening. It is {ancestor}'s surname. {npc} is {ancestor}'s {anc_gen}, and badly fed, and holding the saber backwards.

effects.log: Over soup {npc} explains: a famine, a debt, a bad idea. You find {him} honest work. {He} keeps the saber, for sentiment.

choices.text: Hand over two taels and a lecture

effects.log: "{ancestor} would be ashamed," you say. {npc} looks at the ground. Then {he} turns the saber the right way round.

ok.log: Three moves and {npc} is sitting in the dirt. "Again," you say. By evening {he} can hold the saber.

fail.log: You slip on loose stones and the backwards saber still hurts. {npc} runs off with nothing, horrified. (-6 health)

events.text: In a market {npc} is selling {ancestor}'s sword for rice. You know the hilt wrapping, the knot {anc_rel} always tied wrong. The price is insultingly low. {npc} does not know what {he} has, or does, and is hungry anyway.

choices.text: Buy it and give it back (6 taels)

effects.log: {npc} takes the sword back with both hands and does not speak. You buy the rice as well. Swords should not be sold for rice.

choices.text: Buy it and keep it (6 taels)

effects.log: You melt nothing. But you strip the old blade for the black iron in its core. {ancestor} would have called that practical.
{npc} raises the price tenfold. A sect quartermaster buys it by noon. The family eats well all winter.

events.text: In a mountain temple a young novice is lighting incense before a memorial tablet. It is {npc}, and the tablet is {ancestor}'s. The line sent one of its own to pray for {anc_rel} forever. {npc} looks very young in grey robes, and very bored.

effects.log: Two sticks of incense, one old and one young hand. {npc} sits up a little straighter. The smoke braids.

choices.text: Tell {him} a story to pass the time

effects.log: You tell {npc} about the time {ancestor} fell in a pig pen. The novice laughs so hard the abbot comes to see.
The abbot bows. {npc} gets an extra blanket this winter. Prayer is easier warm.

events.text: At a town contest a young fighter uses {ancestor}'s style. The footwork is unmistakable: two steps, a hop, then that ugly sideways strike {anc_rel} invented. It is {npc}. {He} is winning, just barely, and doing the hop wrong.

choices.text: Shout the correction from the crowd

effects.log: "Higher on the hop!" {npc} hears, adjusts, and wins. Afterwards {he} looks for the voice. You are buying dumplings.

choices.text: Watch the whole bout in silence

effects.log: Watching it again after {anc_years} years, you finally see what {ancestor} was trying to do. You wish you could say so.

choices.text: Find {him} afterward and show {him} the hop

effects.log: {npc} gets it on the twentieth try. "Who taught you?" {he} asks. "The one who taught you," you say.

events.text: A rope creaks on a cliff. Someone is gathering herbs on the face of it, and the rope is fraying. It is {npc}, {ancestor}'s {anc_gen}. {He} has not noticed the rope. {ancestor} never noticed things either.

ok.log: The rope goes as your hand closes on {npc}'s collar. On the ledge {he} hands you the herb. "Fair price," {he} says, shaking.

fail.log: You get there, but land badly. {npc} is safe. Your ankle is not. (-8 health)

effects.log: {npc} grabs the rock just as the rope parts. {He} climbs down cursing. {ancestor} cursed exactly like that.

events.text: A caravan master offers you a seat on the last wagon. It is {npc}, {ancestor}'s {anc_gen}. The family went into trade after {anc_rel} died. {npc} has a ledger in one hand, a whip in the other, and {ancestor}'s squint.

choices.text: Ride along and guard the wagons

effects.log: Two weeks on the road. One bandit attack, quickly over. {npc} pays you guard's wages, exactly, and adds a jar of pickles.
The drivers ask for the one about {ancestor} and the river spirit four times. {npc} pretends not to listen and laughs anyway.
You wave the caravan on. The dust settles. Walking alone has its own company.

events.text: A small wayside shrine stands where {ancestor} once saved a village. {npc} is repairing its roof. The carved figure inside is meant to be {anc_rel}. It looks nothing like {ancestor}. It looks rather like you.

effects.log: An afternoon of tiles and mud. The shrine is dry again. {npc} offers you the first stick of incense. You light it for both faces.
{npc} squints at the figure, then at you. "Oh," {he} says. "Oh no." The carver was apparently paid in rumours.
A rice cake on the little altar. You bow to the statue that is maybe you. It feels very strange. You walk faster.

events.text: Rain drives you into a woodcutter's shelter. Someone is already there: {npc}. You talk for an hour before the surname clicks. {ancestor}'s {anc_gen}. {npc} realises it at the same moment, from something you said about {anc_rel}. The rain gets louder.

choices.text: Keep talking until the rain stops

effects.log: It rains all night. By morning you know three generations of gossip. {npc} knows your worst joke.

choices.text: Share your food and your fire

effects.log: Dried persimmons and a small fire of your qi. {npc} warms {his} hands. "{ancestor} said you were mean with food." You were.

choices.text: Breathe with the rain in silence

effects.log: {npc} falls asleep against the wall. You sit up with the rain, keeping watch, as you once did for {ancestor}.

events.text: A pass guard asks your name for the register, then stops writing. {npc} has heard it from {his} grandmother: the name of the one who knew {ancestor}, {anc_rel}. "You should be dead," {npc} says, then blushes. "Forgive me. Very long dead."

effects.log: "I hear that a lot," you say. {npc} waves you through and forgets to charge the toll.
"That you were kind and impossible." It is a fair verdict. You would like to have known the grandmother.

choices.text: Pay the toll and give a false name

effects.log: {npc} writes down a name you made up. In a hundred years a scholar will search for it. Good luck to the scholar.

events.text: From a cloud terrace of the Upper Realm you can see the world below, if you squint through a hundred years. Down there {npc}, {ancestor}'s {anc_gen}, is lighting incense for {anc_rel}. And then, after a pause, a second stick for you. {He} thinks you are dead.

choices.text: Send a breath of wind to the incense

effects.log: The smoke bends once, politely, toward the sky. {npc} sees it and drops the matches.

choices.text: Watch until the stick burns out

effects.log: It takes as long as incense takes. In the Upper Realm that is no time at all. It feels long.

choices.text: Look away: they have their own lives

effects.log: You turn back to the clouds. The line is in its own hands. That is a mercy for everyone.

events.text: A prayer reaches the Upper Realm with your name on it. The clerk of petitions brings it, sniffing: it is from {npc}, {ancestor}'s {anc_gen}. It asks for rain on a field, a cure for an ox and, if convenient, a husband for a cousin. {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, would have asked for less, and more rudely.

effects.log: Three days of soft rain on one field only. The neighbours are furious. {npc} lights a very large candle.
The ox recovers. It is a stupid ox. {npc} is delighted. The cousin is on their own.

choices.text: File it: the dead are not shopkeepers

effects.log: The clerk approves. You do not feel good about it. The rain comes anyway, eventually, as rain does.

events.text: Far below, {npc} sits in meditation in a cave and is about to break through. You can feel it from here, like a string about to snap. {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, never managed this. The line has climbed one rung higher than its root. The qi is wild.

ok.log: A thread of your qi slides down a thousand miles and steadies {npc}'s heart. The breakthrough lands clean. {He} will never know why.

fail.log: Too much, too far. {npc} breaks through anyway, roughly, coughing blood. Some ladders must be climbed alone.

effects.log: {npc} breaks through on the third try, alone, as you once did. That is the only kind that holds.
You speak the news into the clouds. It is a foolish thing to do. You do it anyway.

events.text: Immortals may walk in the dreams of the living, if they are careful. You walk into {npc}'s. It is a dream of {ancestor}'s old kitchen, which {npc} half remembers and half imagined. {npc} is sitting at the table, waiting for someone. Apparently for you.

effects.log: Dream rice tastes like memory. {npc} asks one question. You answer it. In the morning {he} will remember only the rice.

choices.text: Leave {him} a gift in the dream

effects.log: A small light in the bowl. When {npc} wakes, {his} meridians are clearer. {He} blames the rice.

choices.text: Step back out before {he} sees you

effects.log: Some doors are better left closed. You walk back up through the dark. The kitchen fades behind you.

events.text: From the clouds you see a mountain pass below and {npc} on it, walking straight into an ambush. Heavenly law forbids interfering with the fates of mortals. Heavenly law did not know {ancestor}, {anc_rel}.

ok.log: A small rockslide, very small, very precise. The ambush is buried to the waist. {npc} walks past whistling.

fail.log: The pebble misses by a mountain. A magistrate below reports an omen. {npc} escapes on {his} own, barely.

effects.log: {npc} fights through, wounded, alive. You watch every blow. Obedience is a heavy thing to carry.

choices.text: Send a dream of warning the night before

effects.log: You are too late for tonight, but the ambush waits for tomorrow. {npc} dreams of wolves and takes another road.

events.text: The Mirror Lake of the Upper Realm shows whatever you think of. You think of {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, and the water shows you {npc} instead, asleep at a desk with ink on {his} cheek. The lake has decided that is the answer.

effects.log: {npc} wakes, wipes the ink, and goes on writing. The lake ripples. You still do not know what the question was.

ok.log: For one breath the water shows {ancestor}, young, laughing at something you said. Then it shows {npc} again.

fail.log: The lake shows {npc} again, stubbornly. Perhaps it knows something you do not.

choices.text: Drop a petal on the water

effects.log: Below, a petal falls from nowhere onto {npc}'s page. {He} presses it in the book. Someday someone will wonder.

events.text: In a hall of the Upper Realm the clerks keep the registers of mortal lines. You find {ancestor}'s. It runs on down the pages: names, births, small deaths. At the bottom, still wet, is {npc}. The clerk says the next line is not written yet.

effects.log: Farmers, a scholar, a thief, a good cook. Nobody famous. All of them, in some way, {ancestor}'s.

choices.text: Ask the clerk to look after {npc}'s page

effects.log: The clerk is offended at the suggestion of favouritism, then puts the register on a higher shelf, away from the damp.
The future is not yours to read. You close the register gently, the way you would close a door on a sleeper.

events.text: In the peach orchards of the Upper Realm the blossom falls up instead of down, except at one tree. Under it the petals sink through the clouds. You follow them with your eyes all the way to {npc}'s roof, the house of {ancestor}'s line.

effects.log: A whole shower of blossom falls on {npc}'s yard. The family will call it an auspicious year. It will be, slightly.

choices.text: Eat a peach under the tree

effects.log: It tastes of every spring you remember, and one you do not. Below, {npc} sneezes.

choices.text: Sit and watch the petals fall

effects.log: Petals are slow. Lines are slow. Immortals are slowest of all. You have time.

events.text: A season in the Upper Realm, and when you look down again {npc} has grey hair. Time runs fast down there, like water off a roof. You missed the wedding, the children and the hard years. {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, would say you were always late.

choices.text: Send a blessing for {his} last years

effects.log: {npc}'s winters are mild from now on, and the cough goes. {He} lives eleven years more than expected, cheerfully.

choices.text: Resolve to look down more often

effects.log: You will forget. Immortals always do. But you resolve it, which is something.

choices.text: Look for the next of the line

effects.log: There is a child in the yard, already. {ancestor}'s ears. The line goes on without asking you.

events.text: A paper sky lantern drifts up past the clouds, which they are not supposed to do. It has your name on it and {ancestor}'s, in {npc}'s careful hand. The family sends one up every year. This is the first one that made it.

choices.text: Catch it and read the message

effects.log: "We are well. The roof leaks. We remember." That is the whole message. It is enough to read three times.
The lantern sinks back to {npc}'s yard still burning, brighter than when it left. The whole village sees. Nobody sleeps.
Higher than the Upper Realm there is something else. Let the lantern find out. Someone should.

events.text: {npc} has been sweeping your courtyard every morning for a month without being asked. Today {he} finally speaks: {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, told the family that you never took the apprentice you should have. {npc} would like to apply. {He} has brought references. They are all from {his} mother.

effects.log: "One year," you say. {npc} bows so low {his} forehead touches the broom. The trial begins at once, with more sweeping.

ok.log: Carry water to the peak in a sieve. {npc} freezes the water with {his} breath on the third try. You are impressed, which you hide.

fail.log: {npc} tries for a week, gives up, and stops coming. You find yourself missing the sweeping.

effects.log: {npc} goes. The courtyard gets dusty again. You were too old to start this. Probably.

events.text: {npc} is a year into training and has stopped improving. {He} does everything right and nothing happens. You recognise it. {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, hit the same wall at the same age, and you were there for that too.

effects.log: {ancestor} broke through by getting furious and kicking a tree. {npc} tries it. The tree wins. The wall cracks anyway.

ok.log: Night practice, cold water, a different stance. In a month the wall is gone. {npc} looks at you like a miracle worker.

fail.log: Nothing works for a season. Then one morning it simply does. You take the credit. So does {npc}.

choices.text: Tell {him} to rest for a month

effects.log: {npc} protests, then sleeps for three days. When {he} starts again, the wall is just a step.

events.text: {npc} beats you in a sparring match. Fairly. You did not hold back, much. {He} stands there with the practice sword, frightened by what {he} has done. It is time. You know it. {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, would be laughing at you.

effects.log: You give {npc} your old travelling cloak. {He} leaves at dawn. A year later the rumours start, all of them good.
A lifetime of notes in a box. {npc} carries it out like an egg. The line of {ancestor} has your art now. That feels right.

ok.log: You win the rematch, narrowly, and both of you laugh. Then you send {him} out into the world anyway.

fail.log: {npc} wins again. You sit in the dust and laugh. The pupil is done. The teacher, apparently, is not.

events.text: On a mountain road {npc} blocks your way. {He} names {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, and the old quarrel, which the family has polished for {anc_years} years until it shines. {He} challenges you. {He} is not good enough yet and knows it. {He} came anyway.

ok.log: {npc} ends up in a stream. You leave {him} there. "Ten years," {he} shouts after you. "I will be back."

fail.log: {npc} gets one cut in before you end it. {He} limps away pleased. "Ten years," {he} says.

effects.log: "Coward," {npc} says. "Patient," you say. {He} swears to come back when you cannot refuse.

choices.text: Ask what {his} family says you did

effects.log: {npc} tells it. It is about one third true. {He} leaves before you can say which third.

events.text: Ten years, as promised. {npc} comes back much better. The fight lasts until the lamps are lit. Neither of you wins. Both of you are bleeding a little. {npc} sits down on the ground and laughs, in {ancestor}'s exact laugh.

effects.log: You sit in the dirt together. {npc} passes you a water gourd without looking. That is new.

choices.text: Tell {him} to come back in ten more

effects.log: "Ten more," you say. {npc} grins, wipes {his} mouth, and limps off. You find you are looking forward to it.

choices.text: Offer to end the grudge here

ok.log: {npc} is quiet a long time. "I will think about it," {he} says. From {him}, that is a treaty.

fail.log: "Not yet," {npc} says, getting up. "Not until I win."

events.text: {npc} finds you with an old letter: {ancestor}'s own account of the quarrel, buried in the family chest. It does not say what the family says. It says {anc_rel} was at least half to blame and knew it. {npc} has read it eleven times.

choices.text: Burn the grudge with the letter

effects.log: The letter burns. The grudge goes up with it, {anc_years} years of it. {npc} breathes out like someone putting down a load.
You say it out loud: your half. {npc} nods. Two halves make an end. The family gets a new story.

choices.text: Say the grudge kept you both sharp

effects.log: {npc} laughs. "Then we spar for fun from now on." You do. It is not the same. It is better.

events.text: {npc} asks you a question nobody else alive can answer: where is {ancestor} buried? The family moved, twice, and lost the grave. Rain has flattened the hills for {anc_years} years. You were there. You think you remember.

effects.log: "Give me a season," you say. {npc} bows. You spend the night trying to remember the shape of a hill.

ok.log: The map comes out of you whole: a river bend, a split rock, three pines. {npc} folds it like a letter.

fail.log: The map is mostly guesses. {npc} takes it anyway. "We will find it together," {he} says.

choices.text: Say it does not matter where

effects.log: "Bow anywhere," you say. {npc} does not agree. {He} goes looking alone.

events.text: You find it: a split rock, three pines, one gone now. Under the brambles a stone with {ancestor}'s name, the letters nearly smooth. {npc} goes down on {his} knees in the mud and starts clearing it with bare hands. You kneel and help.

choices.text: Recut the name on the stone

effects.log: Your finger and your qi cut the letters deep and clean. They will last another {anc_years} years, at least.
{npc} listens with mud to the elbows. {He} asks no questions. Some answers are complete.

choices.text: Plant a new pine for the one that fell

effects.log: Three pines again. In a few years nobody will be able to lose this grave. You will make sure.

events.text: {npc} is to marry into the sect where you trained as a youth, and the sect has a custom: an elder of the groom's or bride's side must speak at the gate. {npc}'s side has nobody old enough. Except you, who knew {ancestor}, {anc_rel}. {npc} asks, red to the ears.
events.arc: A Wedding in the Old Sect

effects.log: {npc} breathes out. Then {he} asks what you will say. You say you will think of something. You have no idea.

ok.log: {npc} is better than you expected. You agree, of course. You would have anyway.

fail.log: {npc} is much better than you expected. You agree, rubbing your wrist.

choices.text: Decline: the sect will not remember you

effects.log: {npc} goes away disappointed. Later you hear the sect does remember you. Not fondly.

events.text: The gate is new, but the step you once tripped on is still there. You stand before the whole sect and speak for {npc}. The old elders stare. One of them, ancient and nearly blind, says your name aloud. It is the cook. The bean porridge is on the wedding menu.
events.arc: A Wedding in the Old Sect

effects.log: You tell them who {ancestor} was and who {npc} is. Nobody in the hall moves. The blind cook nods all the way through.

choices.text: Speak about your own years here

effects.log: You tell the sect about the porridge, the beatings, the rooftop. The young disciples are horrified. The old ones laugh until they cry.

choices.text: Keep it short and eat the porridge

effects.log: Twelve words and a bow. Then you eat the porridge. It is terrible. You have two bowls.

events.text: The house of {ancestor}'s line is being sold for debt. {npc} stands in the yard counting tiles that will belong to someone else on the first of the month. You ate many meals in that kitchen with {anc_rel}. The persimmon tree is still there.

choices.text: Pay part of the debt (10 taels)

effects.log: It buys a season. {npc} takes it with shame and gratitude, both. "I will pay it back," {he} says. You believe {him}.

choices.text: Find out who holds the debt

ok.log: The lender is a crook with a forged contract. You know a magistrate. The first of the month comes and goes.

fail.log: The lender is honest and the debt is real. That is worse. You will have to think of something else.

effects.log: You carry boxes. {npc} takes a cutting from the persimmon tree. The house belongs to strangers by spring.

events.text: {npc} has a plan to keep the house: brew {ancestor}'s old rice wine and sell it. The recipe is lost. You remember the taste, and that {anc_rel} put something in it that made strong people weep. You spend a week in the storehouse trying to remember what.

ok.log: Burnt barley and a pinch of pine. The first jar is perfect. {npc} tastes it and weeps, as predicted.

fail.log: It is not the same wine. It is still good wine. It sells. Memory is not a recipe.

effects.log: Your wine is smoother. {npc} names it after you. It sells slower. Novelty is a hard trade.
The oldest porter on the road. Customers buy out of curiosity. They come back for the wine.

events.text: The debt is paid. {npc} hangs a new signboard over the old gate: the family wine house. The persimmon tree is in fruit. {npc} pours the first cup, of tea, for you, the second on the ground for {ancestor}, and the third for {him}self, with shaking hands.

choices.text: Raise your cup to the house

effects.log: The tea is good and the persimmons are better. {npc} cannot stop smiling. Neither, it turns out, can you.

choices.text: Refuse repayment of what you gave

effects.log: {npc} tries to give the ten taels back. You put them in the persimmon tree's roots. "Feed the house."
Small, low, where a child would see it first. {npc} touches it every morning after that.

events.text: On the road a young scholar falls into step with you, notebook out. It is {npc}, writing the chronicle of {ancestor}'s line, and {he} has been searching for you for two years. {He} has a long list of questions. Question one: did {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, really steal an emperor's horse.

effects.log: It takes three days of walking. Yes, the horse. No, not the emperor's. {npc} fills two notebooks and has blisters.
You leave out the horse. {npc} notices and says nothing. {He} is already a good historian.
A question per mile. {npc} gets fit and gets the truth. {He} complains about both.

events.text: The chronicle arrives, bound in silk. You are in it, near the middle, and at the end. The last page is blank except for a line in {npc}'s hand: "To be finished by the one who outlives us all." {npc} has sent a brush with it.

effects.log: You write one page about {ancestor}, {anc_rel}, and one line about {npc}. You send it back. It is the best thing you have written.

choices.text: Leave it blank: the line is not finished

effects.log: You send it back with a note: "Not yet." {npc} understands. The page stays blank for the next {anc_gen}.
In the margin: "It was a mule. It bit me." {npc} prints the second edition with your note. It sells twice as well.
